 Nvidia Filings: $21B+ Billed to Singapore Shipped Elsewhere
 AI Business Brief / By 
 Gennaro Cuofano 
 / November 11, 2026 
 Nvidia ’s Form 10-K for fiscal 2025 put $23,684 million of that year’s revenue in Singapore, counted by where customers were billed, and said “Shipments to Singapore were less than 2% of fiscal year 2025 total revenue ”. On total revenue of $130,497 million, that caps shipments to Singapore at under $2,610 million, so more than $21,074 million billed to Singapore went to other places, at least 88.9% of the Singapore line, by our arithmetic.
 The Kobeissi Letter said on X on 11 November that Nvidia ’s head of PR contacted it within 24 hours of its January 2025 analysis of the Singapore figures. As quoted by Kobeissi, the message said “Our public filings report ‘bill to’ not ‘ship to’ locations of our customers”. We have not seen that message ourselves; the 10-Q sentence it cites does appear, word for word, in Nvidia’s filings.
 Short explainer · Bill-to vs ship-to
 A Business Pill Short that uses this story as its worked example. Facts: Nvidia’s Form 10-K for fiscal 2025 put $23,684 million of revenue in Singapore by customer billing location and said shipments to Singapore were less than 2% of total revenue ; more than $21,074 million billed there therefore went elsewhere, by our arithmetic.
 Business Pill · Concentration
 A short explainer on concentration, when a few big pieces make most of a total. It teaches the general idea and does not discuss Nvidia’s Singapore figures.
 The key insight: As we read Nvidia’s fiscal 2025 10-K, $23,684 million was billed to customers in Singapore while shipments to Singapore were under 2% of $130,497 million of revenue : more than $21,074 million billed there went elsewhere, by our arithmetic.
 Table of Contents
 Toggle 
 Ten Quarters of the Singapore Line 
 What Nvidia Said Actually Shipped There 
 Then the Singapore Line Went Away 
 Why the Billing Question Is Back 
 The Structural Read 
 Three Implications 
 The Business Engineer Lens 
 What Is Not Established 
 The Bottom Line Related 
 Ten Quarters of the Singapore Line 
 Nvidia’s quarterly filings show the Singapore billing line growing faster than the company. It was $762 million, or 10.6% of revenue , in the quarter to April 2023. It reached $7,697 million, 21.9%, in the quarter to October 2024, and $10,156 million in the quarter to July 2025, which the 10-Q for that quarter says was 22% of revenue . All other shares are our arithmetic from the reported tables.
 The two January quarters are our arithmetic, the full year less nine months: $2,325 million, or 10.5%, in the quarter to January 2024, and $6,328 million, 16.1%, in the quarter to January 2025. Over the last four quarters reported on the billing basis, October 2024 to July 2025, Singapore came to $33,198 million, 20.1% of $165,218 million of revenue , by our arithmetic.
 Kobeissi’s figures check out against the filings. It said that in the three quarters before its analysis , $17.4 billion of revenue came from Singapore against $11.6 billion from China. Nvidia’s 10-Q for the quarter to October 2024 gives $17,356 million for Singapore and $11,574 million for China (including Hong Kong) for the first nine months of fiscal 2025.
 Business Engineer the Map of AI — 200+ companies across 9 layers Read → 
 Revenue billed to customers in Singapore as a share of Nvidia’s quarterly revenue , quarters to April 2023 through July 2025, from the billing-location tables in Nvidia’s 10-Qs and 10-Ks. Shares, and the two January quarters (full year less nine months), are our arithmetic. Nvidia switched to a headquarters count, with no Singapore row, from the quarter to October 2025. 
 Animated: revenue billed to customers in Singapore as a share of Nvidia’s quarterly revenue , quarters to April 2023 through July 2025, from the billing-location tables in its 10-Qs and 10-Ks. Shares and the January quarters are our arithmetic. 
 What Nvidia Said Actually Shipped There 
 The filings describe the Singapore shipments in four different ways. The 10-Q for the quarter to April 2024 said “most of the shipments associated with Singapore revenue went to either the United States or Taiwan in the first quarter of fiscal year 2025” and that “Shipments to Singapore were insignificant”.
 The next two 10-Qs, for the quarters to July and October 2024, used the sentence Kobeissi says Nvidia’s PR team quoted: “most shipments associated with Singapore revenue were to locations other than Singapore and shipments to Singapore were insignificant”. The fiscal 2025 10-K added the only number, the under-2% ceiling, and said “Customers use Singapore to centralize invoicing while our products are almost always shipped elsewhere”.
 The first two 10-Qs of fiscal 2026 changed the measure. The one for the quarter to July 2025 says “Over 99% of controlled Data Center compute revenue billed to Singapore was for orders from U.S.-based customers for the second quarter and first half of fiscal year 2026”. That sentence is about who placed the orders, and it covers controlled Data Center compute revenue , not every dollar billed to Singapore.
 Nvidia’s fiscal 2025 revenue by customer billing location, and the 10-K’s ceiling on shipments to Singapore (less than 2 percent of total revenue ). The under-$2,610 million ceiling and the over-$21,074 million shipped elsewhere are our arithmetic. Source: NVIDIA Form 10-K for fiscal 2025. 
 Then the Singapore Line Went Away 
 From the 10-Q for the quarter to October 2025 , Nvidia counts revenue by where customers are headquartered, and the table has no Singapore row. Its footnote says billing location “often reflected a customer’s centralized invoicing location, even though our products were almost always shipped elsewhere”, and that “We believe changing to revenue based upon the location of our customers’ headquarters provides a better representation of the geographic profile of our revenue ”.
 The latest 10-Q, for the quarter to July 2026 , keeps the headquarters count and says “The end customer and shipping location may be different from our direct customers’ headquarters location”. What the recount did to the US and China lines is in our piece on the recast tables and our piece on China revenue under the new count .
 Update, 12 Nov (The Wall Street Journal; Nvidia 10-Qs and 10-Ks on EDGAR). A Wall Street Journal article published on 11 November says that as recently as the summer of 2025 Singapore was officially one of Nvidia’s biggest markets, generating 22% of revenue , and that “practically overnight, it disappeared from the company’s financial disclosures”. Its subheading says Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore revenue just as scrutiny of Megaspeed was rising, and the article argues that investors deserve to know why. We read the part of the article outside the paywall.
 The filings match its figures. The last 10-Q with a Singapore row , filed on 27 August 2025 for the quarter to 27 July 2025, put $10,156 million there, up from $5,622 million a year earlier, and said Singapore was 22% of that quarter’s revenue . For the first half of fiscal 2026 it gave $19,173 million, 21% of $90,805 million. Those six months already came to 81% of the $23,684 million billed to Singapore in the whole of fiscal 2025, by our arithmetic.
 The next 10-Q , filed on 19 November 2025, counts revenue by customer headquarters and says: “We believe changing to revenue based upon the location of our customers’ headquarters provides a better representation of the geographic profile of our revenue .” By our search of each document on EDGAR, the word Singapore does not appear in that 10-Q or in the three reports filed since: the 10-K for fiscal 2026 and the 10-Qs for the quarters to April 2026 and July 2026 .
 The filings do not mention Megaspeed. The policy side is in our pieces on Treasury and Commerce statements on the Nvidia buyer , the H200 buyer on the US blacklist and the debate over Nvidia’s China curbs .
 Why the Billing Question Is Back 
 Kobeissi’s 2025 analysis also compared data-centre counts: about 5,375 in the US, 448 in China and 99 in Singapore, by its figures, which we have not checked. Its post says that analysis raised concerns that chips were potentially being routed to China through Singapore, and that it is not yet established whether the shipments now reported were connected to the figures it highlighted.
 The Financial Times has reported on Singapore’s role in China’s AI chip trade. Our coverage of the policy side: what is on record about Megaspeed and two US-cleared H200 firms in China with empty offices . The market side is in our piece on Nvidia’s 2026 drawdown .
 The Structural Read 
 As we read the filings, the Singapore line measured where invoices were sent, and Nvidia said so in each filing: the share of revenue it carried rose from 10.6% in the quarter to April 2023 to 21.9% in the quarter to October 2024, by our arithmetic.
 As we read the sequence of disclosures, the wording moved from shipments that were “insignificant” to a numeric ceiling in the 10-K, then to a statement about who placed controlled Data Center orders, and then the Singapore row was replaced by a headquarters count.
 As we read it, the headquarters count answers a different question again: the latest 10-Q says the end customer and shipping location may differ from the headquarters location, so none of the three measures shows where every product was used.
 NVIDIA Form 10-K for fiscal 2025, filed 26 February 2025
 “Customers use Singapore to centralize invoicing while our products are almost always shipped elsewhere.”
 Three Implications 
 FOR READERS OF THE FILINGS Billing, shipping, ordering and headquarters locations are four different measures; the Singapore figures in Nvidia’s filings mix the first three.
 FOR THE FISCAL 2025 NUMBERS Of $23,684 million billed to Singapore, under $2,610 million shipped there, by our arithmetic from the 10-K ceiling.
 FOR THE RECENT QUARTERS Since the quarter to October 2025 the tables show no Singapore row; revenue is counted by customer headquarters.
 The Business Engineer Lens 
 This story maps onto the Business Engineer framework AI’s Geopolitical Chokepoint .
 The framework argues the AI supply chain is “creating geopolitical leverage that operates independently of who has the best models”.
 As we read it, how chip sales are counted by country is one place that leverage becomes visible to policymakers. The essay does not discuss Nvidia’s Singapore figures.
 What Is Not Established 
 The filings give a number for shipments to Singapore only for fiscal 2025, and only as a ceiling, so the $21,074 million is a minimum for that year. For the other quarters the wording is “insignificant” or the 99% order statement, which covers controlled Data Center compute revenue only. The filings we read describe billing, shipping and ordering locations, not where every product was finally used.
 Nothing in the filings ties the Singapore line to any investigation or to any customer. Nvidia’s message to Kobeissi is as quoted by Kobeissi, and the data-centre counts are Kobeissi’s. The Financial Times report is cited by its headline only; we have not read its text.

 The Bottom Line 
 Nvidia billed $23,684 million to Singapore in fiscal 2025 while its 10-K put shipments to Singapore at less than 2% of $130,497 million of revenue : more than $21,074 million billed to Singapore went elsewhere, by our arithmetic. The Singapore line peaked at 21.9% of quarterly revenue , by our arithmetic, before Nvidia dropped it for a headquarters count in late 2025.
